# A bill whose line is booked to an equity account, applying a split on that
# same equity account.
#
# `Entry.SetBillAccount` places no restriction on the account, so a bill's
# line can be booked to equity just as a vendor rebate's is booked to income.
# The account test a bill's expense split relies on is then satisfied — the
# bill's posting books `Equity:Owner Contributions USD` — and it must still
# be refused.
#
# What this allowance rests on is that a cost is a cost whichever entry
# carries it. Capital is not a cost, so moving the split to the payable would
# take the capital off the balance sheet with every figure still balancing.
#
# Equity remains a payment account: the owner settling a supplier out of
# their own money is supported, and there `account:` states the equity
# account, which is never the side that moves.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal, with the capital still on the equity
# account.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-CAPITAL-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-03-20
  entry:
    date: 2026-03-20
    description: "Booked to capital"
    account: "Equity:Owner Contributions USD"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-03-20
    due: 2026-04-20
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-CAPITAL-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-20
    amount: 100
    account: "Liabilities:Credit Card USD"
    txn_guid: "5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b"
    txn_split_guid: "6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c"
